articles.title: The Universe's Deepest Laws May Be Fine-Tuned for Flowing Liquids—and Life
articles.summary: New research suggests that fundamental physical constants are locked in a narrow range that keeps liquids like water and blood flowing just right for life. A shift of a few percent could make blood too thick or thin, breaking cellular function. The study shifts fine-tuning arguments from stars to living cells.

articles.title: Catch the Milky Way's Dazzling Core at Its Peak This May
articles.summary: The moonless nights of mid-May offer a prime window to see the Milky Way's core arching across the spring sky. With the new moon, darkness lasts longer than in June, when summer twilight shortens viewing. Head to a dark site, face south, and look between midnight and dawn for the best show.

articles.title: Accidental Discovery: Pond Organism Breaks the Universal Rules of DNA
articles.summary: A protist from an Oxford pond has reassigned two stop codons to different amino acids—a combination never seen before. Normally, TAA and TAG change together, but this ciliate uses them for lysine and glutamic acid. The find challenges the idea of a nearly universal genetic code.
